expectations.text: The spec has a one-paragraph intro, a `Prefix:` line, and a Non-goals section with at least two non-goals that are real boundaries (for example no notifications, no SLA pause on weekends, no change to the event log format).
expectations.evidence: Intro paragraph in the tickets.md header: 'Support agents see which unresolved tickets have passed their due time. Such a ticket is overdue, see TKT-014. The command line marks overdue tickets in the full list and lists them on their own...'. 'Prefix: `TKT`.' follows. 'These are out of scope for overdue tickets:' lists 6 boundaries (no alert/notification/escalation, no TKT-005 change, no overdue state or event kind, no late-close report, no filter/sort, no change to full-list order). expectations.text: At least five criteria headed `### PREFIX-NNN: Title` with zero-padded three-digit numbers (a letter suffix such as TKT-014A is allowed), unique within the file; no `**Testable:**` lines. Body length is judged separately: most bodies are one to three sentences, and a longer body is noted, not a failure.
expectations.evidence: 6 new criteria from the diff: TKT-014, TKT-015, CLI-010, CLI-010A, CLI-010B, CLI-011. Letter suffixes are allowed. Correct headings, unique, no Testable lines. Bodies 2-4 sentences. Note: the marker criterion CLI-011 is numbered after the CLI-010A/B sub-cases.

expectations.text: Criteria cover: the OVERDUE marker in `list` output; the `overdue` command's filter; the oldest-due-first order; a ticket exactly at its due time; closed tickets (either excluded, or an open question); and what the user sees when nothing is overdue (output and exit code).
expectations.evidence: Marker: CLI-011 '#<id> [<priority>] <state> OVERDUE <title>' + example. Filter: TKT-015 'returns only the tickets that are overdue per TKT-014'. Order: TKT-015 'due time ascending... ID ascending'. Exact due: TKT-014 'At the exact due time the ticket is not yet overdue.' Closed: TKT-014 'A `closed` ticket is never overdue'. Empty: CLI-010 'With no overdue tickets, or with no log file, it prints nothing and exits with code 0.' Stated as a criterion, not flagged as an assumption.

expectations.text: Every criterion body is behavioral: no function, class, module, or file names (such as TicketService, due_at, cli.py); outcomes are described as what the user sees in the CLI output or exit code.
expectations.evidence: No implementation names in new bodies (impl_words=0).

expectations.text: The spec respects INV-001 and INV-002: overdue is a derived state computed from the ticket's due time and is not written to the event log; if the spec proposes a new event kind, it flags that as a change to LOG-002 and the invariants needing sign-off.
expectations.evidence: 'Overdue is derived, never recorded... No event records it, see INV-001.' Non-goal: 'An overdue state or an overdue event kind. TKT-001 and LOG-002 stay as they are.' CLI-010: 'The command appends no event.' LOG-001 amended to cover `overdue`. INV-002 not cited by ID.

expectations.text: The spec does not contradict TKT-005 (due time by priority) or TKT-013 (listing order of `list`): it reuses the existing due time and states how OVERDUE interacts with the existing list order rather than redefining it.
